why_not_production: The only deployed environment, readypick-pilot, holds three tenants and thirty jobs and ZERO candidates, profiles, applications and reports (docs/verification/AI_UPGRADE_BASELINE.md, 2026-09-09). context_chunks holds zero rows because services/rag/index.index_document has no caller. A production corpus therefore cannot be drawn, and this corpus is hand authored so the retrieval metrics have a fixed corpus to hold constant, which is the BrowseComp-Plus idea W7.1 is built on. It is NOT a production sample and no case in this set claims to be.

chunks.text: Backend Engineer, payments. Must have production Kafka experience and be able to reason about consumer group rebalancing under partition change.
Nice to have: exposure to Postgres logical replication and to schema migrations executed without downtime.
Behavioural: the engineer is expected to raise a risk before it becomes an incident rather than after.
Reduced payment settlement lag from nineteen minutes to under four by resizing the Kafka consumer group and pinning partition assignment to the settlement key.
Strong team player with a proven track record of delivering high quality software in fast paced environments.
Ran a Postgres major version upgrade across eleven databases using logical replication, with a documented cutover and a tested rollback.
Familiar with distributed systems, microservices, cloud platforms and modern engineering practices.
When the consumer group stalled we found the rebalance was triggered by a slow poll rather than by a broker failure, so we raised max poll interval and cut the batch size.
I flagged the replication lag to the on call channel two days before the release because the write volume was already tracking above what we had load tested.
Public repository: a partition assignor implementation with property tests covering rebalance under broker restart and under consumer restart.
Public repository: a migration runner that refuses a migration lacking a down step, with a test suite exercising interrupted migrations.
Former platform lead confirms the settlement latency work was owned end to end by this engineer and that the rollback plan was exercised in staging.
Expert in Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, Go, Rust, Python, TypeScript, GraphQL and machine learning.
I have not used logical replication myself. I have read the runbook for it and I would want a second pair of eyes the first time.
Wrote the incident review for a four hour payment outage, including the two contributing changes and the detection gap that let it run for ninety minutes.
The hardest part was telling the product owner that the date was wrong. I brought the revised estimate and the two things I had cut, not just the bad news.
Engineering Manager, platform. Must have run a team through a reorganisation while keeping delivery commitments visible and honest.
Nice to have: has built a hiring loop and can describe how it changed the shape of the team.
Behavioural: gives a direct report difficult feedback early rather than letting it accumulate to a review cycle.
Merged two platform teams of six and four, kept the roadmap public through the merge, and lost one person over eight months against a company average of three.
Passionate people leader focused on empowering teams to deliver world class outcomes.
Rebuilt the backend hiring loop around a paired debugging exercise, cutting time to offer from forty one days to twenty three across nineteen hires.
I told him in the first week that the design reviews were not landing, gave him two specific examples, and we agreed a check in every Friday rather than waiting for the cycle.
During the merge I published the delivery dates I believed rather than the ones I had been given, and I said which two I expected to miss.
The hiring loop change was mostly my manager's idea. My part was running the calibration sessions and writing the rubric.
The previous director confirms the two team merge and that attrition through it was one person, and adds that the roadmap was published weekly throughout.
Public write up: the paired debugging exercise used in the hiring loop, with the rubric and the calibration notes.
Managed large cross functional teams and drove significant improvements in velocity and morale.
I have never run a reorganisation. I have been through two as a lead and I watched how the second one handled the people who were reassigned.
Introduced a weekly written delivery note naming what slipped and why, which the two teams kept using after the merge closed.
The feedback I regret is the one I saved for the review. By then he had repeated it four times and it read as an ambush.
VP Engineering. Must have owned a multi year platform migration with a stated cost and a stated benefit, both measured after the fact.
Nice to have: has run an engineering budget through a contraction and can name what was protected and what was cut.
Behavioural: publishes a decision that later proved wrong together with what the decision rested on.
Led a three year migration off a shared monolith database, measured at fourteen engineer years spent against a reduction in change failure rate from eleven percent to three.
Held headcount flat through a nineteen percent budget reduction by ending two internal tools programmes and moving their owners onto the migration.
Visionary technology leader with a track record of driving transformational change at scale.
The build versus buy call on the feature store was wrong. We spent eleven months on it and I wrote up the two assumptions that did not hold, one of which I had been warned about.
In the contraction I protected the on call rotation and the migration, and I cut the internal developer portal, which was the thing I personally wanted most.
The former chief executive confirms the migration ran three years, confirms the change failure numbers were reported to the board quarterly, and confirms the feature store write up was circulated.
Published conference talk with the migration's cost model, including the engineer year accounting and what it excluded.
Responsible for engineering strategy, architecture, delivery, hiring, culture, security and vendor relationships.
I did not own the budget. I proposed the reductions and the chief financial officer decided which of them happened.
Ran a quarterly written review naming every architectural decision reversed that quarter and the evidence that reversed it.
The migration's benefit case rested on change failure rate, and I would use lead time instead now, because change failure rate moved partly for reasons the migration did not cause.
Chief Technology Officer. Must have carried a technology position into a board decision that went against the executive team's preference.
Nice to have: has taken a company through a regulated audit of its data handling.
Behavioural: separates what the company knows from what it believes when reporting to a board.
Argued against the proposed acquisition of a data vendor on integration grounds, lost the first vote, and was asked to run the integration review that reversed it four months later.
Took the company through its first external audit of candidate data handling, closing eleven findings of which three required a schema change.
Seasoned executive with deep expertise across the technology landscape and a passion for innovation.
I told the board we had one quarter of evidence and three quarters of assumption, and I labelled which of the four numbers on the slide was which.
The audit found we were retaining raw assessment media past what the consent covered. We deleted it and changed the pipeline so deletion happens after the verification, not before it.
The board chair confirms the acquisition position was carried against the executive team's preference and that the integration review was commissioned as a result.
Published post on separating measured from assumed numbers in a board pack, with the template the company adopted.
Board level technology leadership including strategy, governance, risk, compliance and organisational design.
I was not in the room for the audit close. My head of data ran it and I read the findings afterwards.
Losing the first vote was the right outcome for the process even though I thought the decision was wrong, and I said so at the time rather than afterwards.
Instituted a board reporting standard in which every figure carries its source and its measurement window, adopted across three functions.
Recognised thought leader in artificial intelligence, cloud transformation and data driven decision making.
